column1: # Accepted cross-line STRUCTURAL differences for scripts/compare_duckdb_lines.sh.
# Without this file the script would be permanently red: the differences below
# are upstream DuckDB behaviour that sitting_duck cannot and should not undo, so
# "fail on any structural drift" would mean "fail forever", and a tool that is
# always red stops being read. Entries here are reported as KNOWN DRIFT and do
# not fail the run; anything structural that does NOT match an entry is
# UNEXPECTED and still fails. Pass --strict to ignore this file entirely.
# An entry is keyed on the SHAPE of the change, never on node_id -- adding one
# statement to a corpus file renumbers every node after it, so an id-keyed
# allowlist would go stale on unrelated edits. An entry matches a changed node
# only when the baseline triple and the candidate triple both match AND no
# other structural column moved; a node that also changed parent, depth or
# descendant count is a different (and unexplained) event, so it is reported as
# unexpected even if its triple matches.
# An entry that matches nothing in a run is reported as a STALE ALLOWLIST ENTRY
# and fails the run: upstream having changed again is exactly the kind of news
# this script exists to deliver, and silently tolerating a dead entry would
# hide it.
# Tab-separated. Empty fields mean "the empty string", not "any value"; there
# are no wildcards, on purpose. Blank lines and #-comments are ignored.
# corpus_file
